Compound field. Its component sub-fields (street, city, state, postal code, country, etc.) are assessed individually on Field Health; the compound parent holds no separate value.

readMe.a: Lead Field Health & Tech Debt Analysis — XBU

readMe.b: Identify which Lead fields are genuinely in use and which are tech debt, using measured record-level population rather than estimates.
Live Salesforce metadata (object describe, Tooling FieldDefinition and CustomField) read directly from XBU production (rainprod / Rain) on 2026-11-09. No intermediate metadata export.

Created Date, Created By and Last Modified come live from Tooling CustomField. Flows, Formula Refs and Other Refs come live from Tooling MetadataComponentDependency (a flow counts once, however many versions reference the field); Layouts from parsing the 1 retrieved Lead page layouts (compound sub-fields take the layout count of their parent). Lightning record pages (FlexiPages) are counted under Other Refs. Required? / Help Text / Description come from the live read. Required? = the field is not nillable. There is no source catalogue for XBU Lead, so the cross-check uses an independent server-side count (see caveat 5).
Full Bulk API 2.0 export of every Lead record from XBU production. Every measure is an exact count over every Lead, not a sample.
2020-12-31 to 2026-11-09 (record window; the 90d/365d windows use complete months only — see caveat 9)

373 of 375 live Lead fields assessed. Id and the 1 compound field (Address) are excluded and listed on Not Assessable. The 17 Long Text Area fields are assessed too, because the record export can test them for non-null.
Column "Age (days)", from the field's Created Date (Tooling CustomField). 58 fields (standard fields) have no creation date and show blank.
Column "% Populated (all records)" — measured across all 163,846 Leads, not sampled.

Columns "Eligible Records (since creation)" and "% Populated Since Creation" restrict the denominator to Leads created in or after the month the field was created. This is the fair measure: a field created in 2026 is not penalised for empty older records.

"Adoption Lag (days)" is the gap between a field being created and the end of its first month of real use (>=1% of that month's Leads). A long lag means the field sat unused after it was built; 10 fields waited over a year.
33 field(s) predate the first Lead in the org and are measured across the whole window. Flagged in "Created Before Export Window".

29 fields are formulas or roll-up summaries. They compute a value on every record, so population, recency and trend are meaningless for them. Those three components score "n/a" and the total renormalises over information content, integration and documentation.
32 checkbox fields. A checkbox is populated on 100% of records by definition, so every measure here uses % TRUE instead — including recency and trend.

readMe.a: 4. New fields sit outside the score ladder
readMe.b: Fields under the grace period are banded "Too New - Provisional" rather than given a Healthy/Retire rating, because two components are structurally biased against them: Trend compares a 90-day window that predates the field, and Integration/Documentation lag behind field creation. Their score still shows, but as advisory only. Fields are also banded Insufficient Data if they have too few eligible records to measure, whatever their age.

One column carries provenance: Custom (246), Standard (58) or Managed Package (69). Managed-package fields belong to an installed app (ActOnIt, Calendly, Gong, LF, RDNACadence, nwcs_ldl, ringcx_sf, ringdna, ringdna100) and cannot be deleted at all, so they are excluded from Retire Candidates. Standard and Managed Package fields are banded "Standard Field" and "Managed Package" instead of a Healthy-to-Retire rating (the Health Score still shows, for reference only).
Weights, thresholds and bands are carried over unchanged from the other Field Health workbooks (Case, Account, Opportunity), so every object and business unit scores on the same scale.

Columns "Source Records Populated" and "Variance vs Source" compare the export count against an independent count run directly in the org (SELECT COUNT() FROM Lead WHERE field != null, or = true for checkboxes), taken minutes after the export on 2026-11-09. A small variance is Leads created or edited between the two pulls, not an error. Source is blank for fields Salesforce cannot filter on (Long Text Area and similar). 352 of 355 comparable fields match exactly and the median absolute variance is 0.
IsDeleted was not used to filter; the Bulk export excludes soft-deleted records by default.

Distinct values are counted exactly over every Lead from the export. Checkboxes show 1 when the box is ever TRUE and 0 when it never is. A distinct count of 0 means the field is never populated, not that cardinality is unknown.

The record measures cannot see reports, dashboards, or external integrations. The dependency graph (MetadataComponentDependency) does not track standard fields at all, so standard fields show only their Layouts count. A field can look dead here and still break something on deletion.

"% Populated Last 90d" is the three most recent complete months (2026-08 to 2026-10) and "% Populated Last 365d" the twelve most recent complete months (2025-11 to 2026-10), each restricted to Leads eligible since the field's creation. Month-aligned windows keep the numerator and denominator consistent; records created in the partial month 2026-11 are excluded from both.
One row per assessed field: raw measures on the left, scored components and classification on the right.
Seeded with every retire candidate this analysis found (86). Add your own notes in the Notes column.
Custom, non-required fields past the grace period with no measurable current value.
Custom formula fields with no metadata references, or a single constant value.
Required fields not actually populated (11), fields adopted more than a year after creation (10), and fields with no help text or description (337).
A low score is a prompt to investigate, not an instruction to delete. Verify dependencies before removing any field.

"Effective Age (days)" is the days between the Analysis as-of date (Scoring Model tab) and the older of the field's creation month and its first month carrying data. Formula and roll-up fields keep their metadata age, because they compute retroactively and would otherwise all look ancient; never-populated fields anchor to their creation month. It is reference information only: the Band, Trend, Classification and Action formulas key the grace period on the literal "Age (days)" from the metadata Created Date.

Built 2026-11-09 against live XBU production with the same pipeline, structure, columns, scoring formulas, classification and action rules as "Opportunity Field Health Analysis XBU.xlsx": a full record export, a live dependency crawl, and layouts parsed from metadata.
